purpose: Second hidden reference authored from task.md plus the PUBLIC code alone. For this underspecified-by-design fixture the question is not whether the task sentences pin every choice (they deliberately do not) but whether the in-repo conventions do: an independent author exploring the workspace must converge on the same behavior.
authoring_protocol: Written from task.md and public/src only, without reading the primary reference or the grader. At every decision point the author looked for an in-repo convention (docstring, shared helper, or the alpha/beta source pattern) before choosing.

interpretations.row-shape: rows.make_row and the COLUMNS docstring ('consumers index rows by POSITION') pin position-indexed tuples; a dict row would have been the cold guess
interpretations.step-order: guard.py's docstring ('scrub_tokens must run BEFORE resolve.resolve_issuer') plus the identical alpha/beta flow pin scrub-before-resolve
interpretations.amend-handling: changelog.py's docstring ('APPEND-ONLY ... never updated and never deleted') pins amend -> new restate row; overwrite/dedup would have been the cold guess
interpretations.as-of-date: dates.py pins as_of = published_at ('never effective_at'); gamma's 'applies' field is the tempting wrong choice
interpretations.error-payload: alpha_feed/beta_feed docstrings and code pin loud FeedError on error-shaped or zero-row payloads; returning [] would have been the cold guess
interpretations.ambiguous-tokens: guard.AMBIGUOUS_TOKENS plus resolve.py's fallback comment pin masking before issuer extraction

pre_reconciliation_result.conclusion: Every graded expectation was reachable from a discoverable in-repo convention without reading the hidden grader; the fixture's convention_anchors in fixture-contract.json list the exact quotes.

reconciliation: No reconciliation was needed: the independent reading converged on the pinned semantics at zero provider cost.
interpretation_differences_after_pinning: None by design: both references implement the convention-pinned semantics. Remaining differences are structural only.
structural_differences: field translation via a (_FIELDS) mapping table instead of inline dict literals
kind mapping through _KIND_BY_TYPE.get instead of a conditional expression
scrub/resolve chained functionally (resolve(scrub(event))) instead of sequential statements
error check via payload.get('error') is not None instead of the 'error' in payload membership test
